The first thing I ever learned to cook---Braised pork chops. Everyone likes these...

Get some thick (1 inch+) bone in pork chops. Sprinkle them with a little flour. Rub them with seasoning salt, garlic powder and pepper, and throw them in a smoking hot skillet with a teaspoon of butter. Sear them for a few minutes on each side, just to get them brown on either side. Meanwhile slice up a yellow onion and have a cup or so of chicken broth ready. When the chops are seared, cover them with the sliced onion and pour the broth into the pan--chops should be about almost covered. if you have some white wine, add about a quarter-cup of that too! Put heat on low, so that it's barely bubbling. Cover the pan tightly (aluminum foil is okay if you don't have a lid that fits) and let simmer for about 10 minutes. Then, flip the chops (If the liquid level gets too low, add a little water to keep from drying out) and cook another 10 minutes or until the chops are cooked through. To test if they are ready, cut into the meat beside the bone; if the juice comes out clear (with no sign of pink) they are done.

When the chops are done, remove them to a plate and boil down the pan juices to make a sauce (the juices can be thickened up by adding a pinch of flour and/or some butter). Add seasoning as needed and serve with rice or vegetable.
